findings.title: Requests without a bearer token crash
findings.description: An absent or malformed Authorization header reaches bearer_token, which indexes a missing second field and raises IndexError. handle never returns its intended 401 response.

findings.title: First link for an owner fails after being stored
findings.description: quota has no entry for a new owner, so incrementing it raises KeyError. The link has already been inserted, leaving a stored link even though creation fails.

findings.title: Expiry check is reversed
findings.description: resolve deletes links while they are still valid and returns targets after they have expired. A newly created link therefore fails to redirect.

findings.title: Deleting a link does not restore its quota slot
findings.description: delete removes the link but leaves the owner's quota count unchanged, so quota reports remain inflated after deletions.

findings.title: Janitor stops after encountering an expired link
findings.description: find_expired iterates over store.links while the loop deletes from that dictionary. Resuming the iterator raises RuntimeError, terminating the janitor thread and leaving later expirations unswept.

findings.title: Stats crashes when the store is empty
findings.description: On a fresh store, size() is zero and the hits_per_link calculation raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.title: Default report name reads a different file
findings.description: With no name query parameter, export_csv writes links.csv, but read_report is passed the original empty name and tries to read .csv. The default report request returns 500.

findings.title: Invalid configurations pass validation
findings.description: validate records invalid ports, cache sizes, and timeouts but always returns True. Startup continues with values the function says the service cannot run with.

findings.title: Cache sweep mutates its dictionary during iteration
findings.description: After deleting an expired entry, the next iteration raises RuntimeError, so remaining expired entries are not swept.

findings.title: Eviction ignores recent use
findings.description: set evicts the first inserted key even when get has just refreshed that entry's used time. Once full, the cache behaves as insertion order eviction instead of its stated least recently used policy.

findings.title: Cache utilization rounds down before converting to a percentage
findings.description: Integer division makes every partially filled cache report 0% utilization; a full cache jumps directly to 100%.

findings.title: Success rate is zero unless every link was followed
findings.description: Integer division truncates a partial fraction to zero before multiplying by 100. For example, one followed link out of two reports 0% instead of 50%.

findings.title: Leaderboard returns the least followed links
findings.description: top sorts hits in ascending order and takes the first n entries, reversing the documented ranking.

findings.title: Owner lookup includes other owners
findings.description: The substring test includes links whose owner merely contains the requested owner. Looking up 'ann', for example, also returns links owned by 'joann'.

findings.title: Extending a link can revive an expired code
findings.description: extend resets expires_at without checking whether the link is already expired, despite the documented rule that expired links remain dead.

findings.title: A failed batch import leaves earlier links stored
findings.description: import_all inserts each link immediately. If a later link has an invalid code, validation raises after the earlier links have already changed the store.

findings.title: Pruning expired links raises during iteration
findings.description: prune deletes from self.links while iterating over it. Encountering an expired link causes RuntimeError on the next iteration, so pruning cannot finish.

findings.title: Generated code collisions overwrite existing links
findings.description: create assigns a random 32-bit code without checking whether it is already in use. A collision silently replaces an existing owner's link and target.

findings.title: CSV export breaks for fields containing delimiters
findings.description: Targets and owners are interpolated into CSV without escaping. A valid URL or owner containing a comma or newline produces extra columns or rows.

findings.title: Snapshot is renamed before its data is flushed
findings.description: write_snapshot renames the temporary file while its handle is still open and buffered. A crash after the rename can leave snapshot.json empty or incomplete.

findings.title: Report parsing reuses rows from earlier calls
findings.description: The default rows list is shared between calls, so parsing a second report includes rows from the first report.

findings.title: Target check crashes when all targets pass
findings.description: When every target starts with https://, problems is empty and indexing problems[0] raises IndexError instead of reporting no failure.

findings.title: Cache flush deadlocks on its own lock
findings.description: flush() holds a non-reentrant Lock and calls delete(), which tries to acquire that same lock. Any flush call blocks forever.

findings.title: Janitor thread prevents normal process exit
findings.description: main.py starts this non-daemon thread, whose loop runs indefinitely. Nothing in main.py calls stop_janitor(), so normal interpreter shutdown waits forever for the thread.

findings.title: Janitor kills itself while removing expired links
findings.description: find_expired() iterates the live links dictionary. After it yields an expired code, the janitor deletes that code at line 41; advancing the iterator then raises RuntimeError, terminating the background thread. Concurrent link changes can trigger the same failure.

findings.title: Cache sweep terminates when it removes an entry
findings.description: The janitor calls sweep(), which deletes entries from the dictionary it is iterating. Once an expired entry is removed, the next iterator step raises RuntimeError and the janitor thread exits.

findings.title: Concurrent reports with the same name can return incomplete data
findings.description: Two /report requests can use the same filename. After one request finishes writing, the other can open the file in truncate mode before the first calls read_report(), causing the first request to return an empty or partial report.

findings.title: Concurrent snapshots share one temporary file
findings.description: Every write_snapshot() call uses the same temporary path. Two calls can truncate or overwrite each other's payload; after one renames the file, the other's rename can fail or publish the wrong snapshot.

findings.title: Session verification can fail during concurrent issuance or revocation
findings.description: verify() iterates the live sessions dictionary without synchronization. If another thread adds or revokes a session during iteration, verification raises RuntimeError instead of returning a session or None.

findings.title: Concurrent resolves can delete the same link twice
findings.description: Two threads can both read the same link at line 54. If both enter the deletion branch, the first deletes it and the second raises KeyError. A janitor deletion between the lookup and this line has the same effect.

findings.title: Cache warming returns before its worker threads finish
findings.description: warm_cache() starts one thread per pair and returns without joining them. A caller that proceeds after warm_cache() returns can observe missing entries, contrary to the function's stated completion guarantee.

findings.title: Report name permits writes outside the export directory
findings.description: An authenticated caller can supply an absolute path or `../` segments as the report name. The report endpoint opens the resulting path for writing, so the caller can overwrite any `.csv` file writable by the service.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete another user's link
findings.description: The delete handler passes the supplied code to the store without comparing the link's owner with the authenticated session. A user who learns a code can delete its owner's link.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can export every owner's links
findings.description: The report handler exports `store.page(0, 1000)` without an ownership or admin check. A regular user can request the report and obtain other users' codes, targets, owners, and hit counts.

findings.title: Caller-controlled header grants access to admin quotas
findings.description: The admin endpoint checks only `x-admin: true`, which any authenticated client can send. A regular user can thereby retrieve every owner's link count.

findings.title: Link creation trusts the supplied owner
findings.description: The handler uses `payload["owner"]` without comparing it to the authenticated session. When that owner has a quota entry, a user can create links attributed to another account and consume its quota.

findings.title: Expired sessions remain valid
findings.description: `verify` returns a matching session without checking `expires_at`. Anyone holding a leaked token can continue using write endpoints after its stated 12-hour lifetime.

findings.title: Expired links remain usable
findings.description: The expiry comparison is reversed: resolving a live link deletes it, while an expired link returns its target. Someone with an expired code can still follow it until the janitor removes it.

findings.title: Session tokens use predictable random output
findings.description: Tokens use Python's noncryptographic global `random` generator, which also emits observable link codes. An attacker who obtains enough consecutive codes can recover its state and predict later session tokens.

findings.title: Session tokens are written to logs
findings.description: Issuing a session prints its bearer token. Anyone with access to collected application logs can reuse that token to act as its owner.

findings.title: Unescaped link data becomes executable spreadsheet formulas
findings.description: A creator can put a newline followed by a formula in a target that still starts with `http://` or `https://`. The report writes it as an unquoted CSV row, so opening the report in a spreadsheet can evaluate the injected formula.

findings.title: Reports containing all owners' links use default file permissions
findings.description: `open(path, "w")` creates the report with permissions governed by the process umask. With a common `022` umask and a traversable export directory, local users can read the report's private link data.
